title: Always open, never enough hands: the strain on Japan's convenience stores

sents.en: Japan's corner shops pay bills, post parcels and print documents at three in the morning.
sents.zh: 日本街角的小店，凌晨三点也能帮你缴费、寄包裹、打印文件。

sents.en: Keeping them that way is getting harder as the people who staff them grow scarce.
sents.zh: 可随着店员越来越难找，要让它们保持这样正变得越来越难。

sents.en: It is two o'clock in the morning in a quiet suburb of Osaka, and the only lights on the street belong to a convenience store.
sents.zh: 大阪一个安静的郊区，凌晨两点，整条街唯一亮着的灯属于一家便利店。

sents.en: Inside, a lone clerk is restocking rice balls, while a taxi driver warms up a bento in the microwave and a student pays her phone bill at the till.
sents.zh: 店里，一个店员独自在补货饭团；一位出租车司机在用微波炉热便当，一个学生在收银台交手机费。

sents.en: Nobody seems to find any of this remarkable.
sents.zh: 没有人觉得这有什么稀奇。

sents.en: Japan has more than 55,000 of these shops, known locally as konbini, or roughly one for every 2,200 people.
sents.zh: 日本有五万五千多家这样的店，当地人叫它们“konbini”，大约每两千二百人就有一家。

sents.en: They began as copies of American corner stores in the 1970s, but have since grown into something closer to a public utility.
sents.zh: 它们在上世纪七十年代起步时是在模仿美国的街角商店，后来却发展成了更接近公共服务设施的东西。

sents.en: Customers can pay taxes and utility bills, send and collect parcels, buy concert tickets, withdraw cash and print official documents such as residence certificates.
sents.zh: 顾客可以在这里交税、交水电煤气费，寄取包裹，买演唱会门票，取现金，还能打印住民票这类官方文件。

sents.en: After earthquakes, the chains are among the first to reopen, and local governments count on them to keep food and water flowing.
sents.zh: 地震过后，这些连锁店总是最早恢复营业的一批，地方政府也指望它们保证食物和饮用水的供应不断。

sents.en: All of this rests on a business model that leaves very little room for error.
sents.zh: 这一切都建立在一种几乎容不得出错的经营模式上。

sents.en: Most stores are run by franchise owners, who pay the parent company a hefty share of their gross profit in return for its brand, its supply chain and its data.
sents.zh: 大多数门店由加盟店主经营。他们把毛利的一大块交给总部，换来总部的品牌、供应链和数据。

sents.en: Lorries deliver fresh food several times a day, so shelves rarely sit empty and little is left to go to waste.
sents.zh: 货车每天送几次新鲜食品，所以货架很少空着，剩下来要浪费掉的东西也很少。

sents.en: The system is famously efficient, but it depends on someone being behind the counter around the clock.
sents.zh: 这套体系的高效出了名，可它要靠柜台后面一天二十四小时都有人。

sents.en: That someone is increasingly hard to find.
sents.zh: 而这个“有人”越来越难找。

sents.en: Japan's working-age population has been shrinking for three decades, and part-time jobs that pay little and involve night shifts are the first to go unfilled.
sents.zh: 日本的劳动年龄人口已经连续三十年在减少，工资低、又要上夜班的兼职工作最先招不到人。

sents.en: Many owners now cover the gaps themselves, working 12-hour shifts for weeks on end.
sents.zh: 许多店主只好自己顶上空缺，一连几周每天上十二个小时的班。

sents.en: A few years ago, an owner who shut his shop overnight without permission, saying he could no longer stay awake, briefly became a national talking point.
sents.zh: 几年前，一位店主没经总部同意就在夜里关了店，说自己实在熬不住了，一时成了全国热议的话题。

sents.en: The chains have responded in several ways.
sents.zh: 连锁总部想了几种办法应对。

sents.en: Foreign workers, many of them students from Vietnam, Nepal and China, now make up a large share of staff in big cities.
sents.zh: 在大城市，外国员工如今占了店员的很大一部分，其中不少是来自越南、尼泊尔和中国的留学生。

sents.en: Self-checkout machines are spreading, and some stores have experimented with closing at night or running without staff at all.
sents.zh: 自助收银机越来越普及，有些店还试过夜里关门，甚至完全不用店员。

sents.en: Yet every shortcut chips away at what made the konbini indispensable in the first place: a real person, ready to help, at any hour.
sents.zh: 可每一种省事的办法，都在一点点削弱便利店当初让人离不开的东西：任何时候都有一个真人在那里，随时可以帮忙。

sents.en: There is a lesson here for other rich countries that are ageing fast.
sents.zh: 这对其他正快速老龄化的富裕国家是个教训。

sents.en: Services that people take for granted are often propped up by cheap, flexible labour that is quietly disappearing.
sents.zh: 人们视为理所当然的服务，往往是靠廉价、灵活的劳动力撑起来的，而这样的劳动力正在悄悄消失。

sents.en: Japan's convenience stores may be the first place where the shortfall shows up, but they are unlikely to be the last.
sents.zh: 日本的便利店可能是最早显出人手短缺的地方，但不太可能是最后一个。

sents.en: Sooner or later, customers may have to accept that convenience, like everything else, has a price.
sents.zh: 迟早，顾客可能得接受一个事实：便利和别的东西一样，也是要付出代价的。
